Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zuutf 0.1.0

First release. zuutf validates and converts text between the Unicode encodings R meets, through a bundled copy of simdutf 9.2.1, and says where the first error is.

Validation and counts

  • utf_valid(), utf_error_at() and utf_is_ascii() check character, raw and list-of-raw input in UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32 (either byte order, or chosen by a byte-order mark), Latin-1 and ASCII, and give the 1-based offset of the first error in the input’s code units.
  • utf_count() counts code points; utf_length_as() gives the bytes a conversion will write.

Conversion

  • utf_convert(), utf_decode() and utf_encode() convert between every pair of UTF-8, UTF-16LE/BE, UTF-32LE/BE and Latin-1. A byte-order mark is read on input and never written. Ill-formed input raises an error, is replaced with U+FFFD as the WHATWG decoder does (? in Latin-1), or gives NA, as invalid says.
  • utf_detect() lists the encodings bytes could be in, a byte-order mark first; utf_decode() uses it by default.

Base64

  • base64_encode() and base64_decode() cover the standard and URL alphabets (either at once on decode with url = NA), padding, line wrapping, and forgiving (WHATWG) or strict (RFC 4648) decoding.

For other packages

  • A registered C table, zuutf_api_v1, declared in the installed header zuutf.h, gives validation, conversion and Base64 to other packages’ C code without vendoring simdutf (vignette("linking")).

Errors and information

  • Every error is a classed condition under zuutf_error (?zuutf_error).
  • zuutf_info() reports the simdutf version, the kernel in use and the kernels compiled in.
